items.rationale: Overvoltage from lightning (2.3.3) is covered, and the endorsement waives the 50% reduction for missing surge protection. Indemnity is the standard-grade replacement price (7.1.9), well within the EUR 5,000 sub-limit. Case 1 implies roughly EUR 1,650 for the pair at full value, so I take about EUR 600 for the speakers.
Carriage and delivery of replacement property are not repair costs under 7.1.8(b), so t = 0.
Fitting, installing and commissioning of replacement property is excluded under 7.1.8(c), so t = 0.

Damage to the TV is established by the diagnostic report and falls under overvoltage cover (2.3.3). The reduction is waived by the endorsement, so indemnity is the standard-grade replacement price with no betterment (7.1.9). Taking the Case 1 pair total of about EUR 1,650 less about EUR 600 for the speakers gives roughly EUR 1,100.

items.description: Property and liability damage to electronics
items.rationale: This charge relates to an arrangement covering liability and property exposure. 3.1.4, 3.1.5 and 7.1.8(f) exclude it, and the liability and property elements are not separately priced, so t = 0.

items.description: Service order for property and liability arrangement
items.rationale: Charges for placing or administering an order under a service or liability arrangement are excluded under 3.1.5 and 7.1.8(f), so t = 0.

Under 7.1.8(d) an attendance charge is covered only when the work on the same invoice is indemnifiable. Lines 5 and 6 on this invoice are not, so t = 0. Case 3 shows the same logic, with a small possible amount if paid.
